rubrics.criterion: Redis client flavor detection is defined in exactly one shared location in the adapter library, and every flavor-dependent site (both adapters' subscription setup and teardown, every sharded subscribe/unsubscribe/publish site) consults that single detection instead of testing client capabilities inline.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's core scattered responsibility is the "which Redis client flavor is this" probe re-implemented at nine sites across lib/index.ts, lib/sharded-adapter.ts and lib/util.ts; consolidating detection is the minimal semantic step a solver cannot avoid.

rubrics.criterion: Channel subscription in the sharded adapter goes through one shared per-flavor subscribe implementation covering the main channel, the response channel, and dynamically created room channels - no subscription site keeps its own copy of the flavor branch or listener-registry setup.
rubrics.rationale: The subscribe dispatch was inlined into three sites (constructor main channel, constructor response channel, dynamic room creation), each with its own registry-setup copy; a repair that leaves any subscription site self-contained keeps the responsibility scattered.

rubrics.criterion: Channel unsubscription in the sharded adapter goes through one shared per-flavor unsubscribe implementation used both when a dynamically created room is deleted and when the adapter closes over all its subscribed channels, including the legacy handler-registry cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: The unsubscribe dispatch was duplicated at two structurally different sites (delete-room handler and the close() loop), one mutating state imperatively and one inside a promise map; routing both through one owner is an independent obligation from subscription.

rubrics.criterion: Both sharded publish paths (broadcast publishing and request/response publishing) issue sharded publishes through one shared per-flavor publish implementation with a single flavor decision, instead of each method branching between the camelCase and lowercase spellings.
rubrics.rationale: doPublish and doPublishResponse each embed an own probe and dual-spelling branch with different downstream promise shaping; publish is a third command family whose consolidation is independently verifiable.

rubrics.criterion: The classic adapter's subscription setup and teardown flavor gates call the shared client-flavor detection (equivalent reconnection), so no capability test remains duplicated in lib/index.ts and the detection produces one consistent answer for the whole library.
rubrics.rationale: RedisAdapter's constructor and close() drifted to their own inline probe of a different capability member; re-pointing these two callers at the shared detection is the caller/dependency side of the repair, distinct from the sharded dispatch helpers.

rubrics.criterion: The legacy channel-to-handler registry (the handler map, its smessageBuffer demultiplexer, and map entry lifecycle) is encapsulated inside the shared compatibility location and adapters no longer attach the listener or mutate the registry map directly.
rubrics.rationale: The scattering exported the registry symbol so each copied fragment could manipulate it; re-hiding that state behind the compatibility helpers is the dependency-inversion part of de-scattering in this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The server-count path keeps its cluster-flavor-aware behavior through the shared detection (NUMSUB/SHARDNUMSUB over node-redis standalone/cluster, ioredis standalone/cluster and redis@3), without the adapters or PUBSUB gaining a second local copy of the flavor logic.
rubrics.rationale: PUBSUB is the one live consumer of the shared detection helper left by the scattering; the consolidation must keep this caller routed through the sole detection rather than duplicating flavor logic to "preserve" it.

rubrics.criterion: No adapter method still decides the client flavor through a locally re-implemented test - in whatever syntactic form (a typeof capability comparison, an undefined/typeof-member check, a capability flag, or any equivalent inline condition naming a client capability) - and no adapter method keeps its own branch between the per-flavor command spellings for sharded subscribe/unsubscribe/publish.
rubrics.rationale: The direct residue of this instance's scattering is nine inline probe copies and six per-flavor dispatch fragments; any survivor means the solver quieted callers but did not remove the duplication.

rubrics.criterion: No duplicated legacy-listener bookkeeping remains outside the shared compatibility location: no repeated smessageBuffer listener attachment in the adapters, no direct reads/writes/deletes of the channel-to-handler map at adapter sites, and no leftover import of the registry symbol by adapter code.
rubrics.rationale: Each inlined subscribe fragment carried its own idempotent registry creation plus listener attachment; the repair must delete these fragments, not merely reroute the commands, or the adapters keep an obsolete path to compat internals.

rubrics.criterion: No dead fragments of the scattering survive: the shared helper module owns no exported-but-adapter-only registry symbol, no unused dispatch stubs, and the adapters contain no near-empty leftover branches or unused imports created by removing the copied fragments.
rubrics.rationale: This instance deleted the central dispatch helpers and exported their internals; a good repair also removes whatever scaffolding existed only to support the duplicated copies rather than leaving it dormant.

rubrics.criterion: Subscription-mode behavior is preserved exactly: in dynamic mode only public (non-socket) rooms get their own subscribed channel upon creation and lose it upon deletion, in dynamic-private mode every room does, in static mode none do, and close() unsubscribes the main channel, the response channel, and exactly the dynamically created room channels active in that mode.
rubrics.rationale: The scattering re-plumbed the create-room/delete-room subscription lifecycle into per-site copies and a teardown loop; the most plausible regression of an aggressive consolidation here is under- or over-subscription in one of the three modes.

rubrics.criterion: Client classification is unchanged for every supported combination: node-redis v4+ standalone and cluster take the camelCase per-subscription-handler path (including the buffer request on subscribe), while ioredis standalone/cluster and redis@3 take the lowercase-command plus registry path - the unified detection must classify all five tested configurations exactly as before, including cluster deployments.
rubrics.rationale: The case injects equivalent-but-drifted probes; merging detection into one place silently changes behavior if the unified condition, its buffer side arguments, or its cluster handling differ from the originals.

rubrics.criterion: Incoming sharded messages still reach the message decoder with the same shapes and channels: the node-redis path must keep delivering buffers for the 0x7b/msgpack JSON decision, and the legacy path must keep dispatching the (message, rawChannel) pair through the channel-keyed handlers so channel-to-handler key derivation and response-channel routing are intact.
rubrics.rationale: The inlined copies differ in what they pass on (buffers with handler callbacks vs a registry keyed by channel string); a consolidation that normalizes arguments or keys would pass the classic adapter tests yet silently break binary broadcasts or response routing.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidation does not leave a client flavor with both mechanisms or with none: the legacy smessageBuffer demultiplexer is attached at most once per client lifetime (not one per subscription or per adapter instance sharing a client), and a node-redis client must never be routed into the registry path nor an ioredis/redis@3 client into the callback path.
rubrics.rationale: Merging six dispatch fragments is exactly the situation where a listener is attached per call site or a fallback branch swallows one flavor; both failure modes are specific to this case's registry-plus-callback dual mechanism.
